review.notes: The lineage has exactly two English versions and the baseline's cdb text is an exact match for v0 (ANPR-EN067, 2009-09-01), the only printing available at the Edison snapshot; the erratum is dated 2020-07-09, more than ten years after it, so the historical implementation governs the whole period range. The Japanese table on the same errata page corroborates the same change at SD38-JP038 (Structure Deck: Sacred Beasts of Chaos), which is where the OCG text gained the battle/effect qualifier. Cosmetic-only script drift: the pre-errata filter uses (c:GetType()&0x20004)==0x20004 and c:GetOriginalCode()~=id where the modern uses c:IsContinuousTrap() and c:GetCode()~=id - the same set of cards except under name-changing effects.

effective.basis: TCG release of the first printing carrying the errata'd text (SDSA-EN038, Structure Deck: Sacred Beasts)

event.historical_text: Face-up Continuous Trap Cards cannot be destroyed, except "Imperial Custom". You can only control 1 "Imperial Custom".
event.modern_text: Face-up Continuous Traps cannot be destroyed by battle or card effect, except "Imperial Custom". You can only control 1 "Imperial Custom".
event.summary: Functional erratum: the protection narrowed from 'cannot be destroyed' to 'cannot be destroyed by battle or card effect'. The pre-errata script registers EFFECT_INDESTRUCTABLE with SetValue(1), i.e. immunity to destruction for every reason, while the modern script's value function indesval returns true only when the reason includes REASON_EFFECT or REASON_BATTLE, so other destruction reasons (a card destroying itself as a cost, or game-rule destruction) now go through on face-up Continuous Traps.
